subject: Telemetry handshake & acceptance criteria — NovaPay onboarding
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Telemetry handshake & acceptance criteria — NovaPay onboarding

Hi Alyssa / Sanjay,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, we want to align on the acceptance telemetry and the handoff package so your SREs and ours can verify the November load run without back-and-forth. Key asks from our side:

- Confirmation of the test profile (clients, qps ramp, mean/peak sequence lengths).
- Attachments with raw tail-latency samples and aggregated throughput by interval.
- Whether you want Redwood to run the simulated traffic from our dedicated pool or if you'll inject from your test harness (or both).

Acceptance gating (proposed):
- 95th percentile latency under 120ms and 99th percentile under 300ms for the production prompt mix at nominal load (5k rps sustained for 10 min).
- End-to-end 1% error rate or lower (includes 5xx and model rejections).
- KV-cache hit rate of >= 60% for warm runs (we'll share cache-warm directives).

If you can send the test artifacts after your Friday run (sample logs, CSV exports, and the JMeter/locust profile), we'll ingest and validate on our side. I've attached our current runbook snapshot for reference.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm which run (Nov 3) is official acceptance run.
2) You share artifacts by EOD Nov 4.
3) Redwood performs validation and returns a pass/fail report with remediation notes by Nov 5.

Thanks — looking to keep this as lightweight as possible so we can sign off and schedule the Dedicated pool for production.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: onboard_runbook_snapshot_v2.docx (runbook snapshot, 42KB)
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novapay.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry handshake & acceptance criteria — NovaPay onboarding

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 09:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alyssa / Sanjay,
>
> Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, we want to align on the acceptance telemetry and the handoff package so your SREs and ours can verify the November load run without back-and-forth.

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Confirming Nov 3 run is our official acceptance attempt. We completed a warmup + three steady-state windows (10 min each) this morning. Quick highlights from our side (see attached CSV and PDF):

- Sustained throughput: 5,200 req/s average during steady windows.
- 95th percentile latency: 108ms. 99th percentile latency: 285ms.
- Error rate: 0.8% (mostly transient 429s from our harness initially; retried).
- KV-cache simulated hit rate: 57% (we did a warm run for 30 minutes prior).

Attached: novapay_throughput_report_2026-11-03.pdf, tail_latency_export_2026-11-03.csv

We ran traffic from our internal harness (GKE-based locust cluster) and also captured wire traces and request IDs to correlate with your logs. If you want us to replay against your Dedicated pool from Redwood's egress, we can coordinate a short window next Tuesday.

Let us know what additional artifacts you need.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
SRE Lead, NovaPay

Attachments: novapay_throughput_report_2026-11-03.pdf (report, 128KB), tail_latency_export_2026-11-03.csv (CSV, 256KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry handshake & acceptance criteria — NovaPay onboarding

Marissa / team,

Saw Alyssa's numbers — thank you. A couple of quick internal checks before we publish the validation:

1) Tail-latency correlation: ask infra to map the 99th percentile spikes to kernel/backpressure events and to the model variant used (we need to confirm quantized vs fp16 fallback instances).
2) Error taxonomy: request Alyssa to annotate the 0.8% with request IDs for the 5xx/429s so we can determine if it's client-side throttling or a server-side transient.
3) KV-warm policy: since their hit rate is 57% (below our proposed 60%), let's run a Redwood-sourced warm run from our Dedicated pool to see if cache polishing increases it above 60% (we should schedule a 20-min warm sequence and re-run).

Ben — can your team provision a 1-hr Dedicated test window next Tue (Nov 9) 09:00–10:00 PST for a combined replay? Ideally we run 10 min warm, 3x10 steady windows and capture the same exports. I'll draft the validation checklist we return to the customer.

I'll collect the artifacts and aim to send the validation report back to NovaPay by EOD Nov 5. If anything looks off, we'll include remediation steps and a proposed follow-up test.

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Customer Success Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novapay.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telemetry handshake & acceptance criteria — NovaPay onboarding

Alyssa / Sanjay — thanks for the artifacts and for running the official attempt. We've completed our validation pass against the exports you shared and our internal replay: summary below. Full validation report is in the shared Drive link.

Validation summary
- Throughput: pass. Your reported 5,200 rps sustained maps to 5,150 rps when we replayed against a Redwood Dedicated replica (within 1% margin).
- Latency: marginal pass. 95th ~110ms, 99th ~290ms in our replay (your CSV and our replay align). Both are under the 'soft' acceptance ceiling (99th < 300ms) but note we are close to the tail bound — see remediation note 1.
- Errors: pass at 0.8% but majority classified as client-side throttling (429) during your initial warm ramp. Once retried, error rate fell below 0.5%.
- KV-cache: fail (57% observed). After a Redwood warm replay the cache hit improved to 66% (we used a 20-min warm with pinned prefixes).

Acceptance decision: CONDITIONAL PASS. NovaPay meets the throughput and error-rate gates. KV-cache was below threshold for your native run, but our warm-replay demonstrates remediation; recommend a final combined run from your harness while we provision the Dedicated replay (Nov 9) to confirm consistent cache behavior under load.

Action items
- Ben: please provision a 1-hr Dedicated test window Tue Nov 9 09:00–10:00 PST (confirm by EOD Mon).
- Alyssa: please annotate the 429/5xx request IDs and share any rate-limiting config that could explain the initial spikes.
- Karthik: please capture kernel-level trace for the 99th spikes and confirm model variant routing for those windows.
- Monica: finalize the short validation report and post to the Drive link below.

Drive (validation artifacts & report): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/novapay/acceptance-artifacts
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/4781/deal/DEAL-4781

If all items above are closed after the Nov 9 combined run, we'll mark onboarding acceptance complete and schedule the Dedicated production carve-out. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
